newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-NO WORLD CUP EVENTS FOR OLYMPIC DOWNHILL COURSE.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NO WORLD CUP EVENTS FOR OLYMPIC DOWNHILL COURSE.

text.p: The men's downhill course built for next year's Winter Olympics will not be used for World Cup events afterwards unless the start is raised ahead of the Games, Marc Hodler, president of the International Ski Federation (FIS), said on Tuesday.
Hodler said other courses could be used for World Cup events following the Games but not the men's downhill.
"It's impossible. Not for the World Cup." Hodler said.
He added that even if the start were raised following the Games, the Hakuba course would still not be considered for World Cup events.
"It would be an invalidation of the Olympics," he said.
Olympic organisers had wanted the start raised from 1,680 to 1,800 metres above sea level but local officials refused because it would encroach on an environmentally sensitive national park.
Hodler said he would not continue to pressure Nagano officials into making a change.
"I'm not going to push," he said. "It should come from the Japanese. We are guests and we try to be polite with our hosts.
"We were told that environmental people are against using the higher start and we don't want to make the Olympic Games the stage for any negative demonstration."
The FIS favours a higher start for the downhill in Hakuba, 50 kms west of Nagano, in order to lengthen the run and include a spectacular jump.
